questions.question: The average production of type D cars in 5 years is what percent less than the production of type E cars in 2018?
questions.solution:
Total production of type D cars in five years = 46 + 50 + 54 + 68 + 67 = 285

⇒ Average production of type D cars in five years = 285/5 = 57

Production of type E cars in 2018 = 70

∴ Required percentage = [(70 – 57)/70] × 100 = 18.6 (Approx)

questions.question: The total production of type B cars in all the five years is what percent more than the total production of type A, B and D cars in 2017?
questions.solution:
Production of type B cars of 5 years = 54 + 45 + 47 + 50 + 40 = 236

Production of cars type A, B and D in 2017 = 43 + 50 + 67 = 160

∴ Required percentage = [(236 – 160)/160] × 100 = 47.5%

questions.question: What is the ratio of the total production of type C cars in 2015 and type D cars in 2017 taken together to the total production of type B cars in 2016 and type A cars in 2017 taken together?
questions.solution:
Production of type C cars in 2015 and type D in 2017 = 53 + 67 = 120 thousands

Production of type B cars in 2016 and type A in 2017 = 47 + 43 = 90 thousands

∴ Required ratio = 120 : 90 = 4 : 3

questions.question: A and B are travelling towards each other from the points P and Q respectively. After crossing each other, A and B take 6(1)/(8) hours and 8 hours, respectively, to reach their destinations Q and P, respectively. If the speed of B is 16.8 km/h, then the speed (in km/hr) of A is:
questions.solution:
If A and B after crossing each other takes x and y hours, respectively, to reach their destinations then the ratio of their speed will be

(Speed of A) / (speed of B) = √(y/x)

According to the question

Speed of A/16.8 = √[8 ÷ (49/8)]

⇒ Speed of A/16.8 = √([8 × 8)/49] = 8/7

⇒ Speed of A = 8/7 × 16.8 = 19.2 km/hr

questions.question: The value of √(sec²θ + cosec²θ) × √(tan²θ – sin²θ) is equal to:
questions.solution:

⇒ √(sec² 45° + cosec² 45°) × √(tan² 45° – sin² 45°)

⇒ √(2 + 2) × √[1 – (1/2)]

⇒ 2 × [1/√2]

⇒ √2

sin θ sec²θ

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 8%. Had he sold it at a gain of 10.5%, he would have received Rs. 92.50 more. To gain 12%, he should have sold it for:
questions.solution:
As we know, the difference between the loss percentage and the gain percentage = 10.5 – (-8)

According to the question

⇒ x × (18.5/100) = 92.50

⇒ x = Rs.500

∴ Required selling price = 500 × [112/100] = Rs. 560.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Given:

Selling price with 8% loss

If 10.5% Gain, then he would get Rs.92.50 more

Desired profit = 12%

Concept used :

Cost Price = Initial Selling Price / (1 - Loss%) and New Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Desired Profit%)

Calculation:

Change from 8% loss to 10.5% gain = 18.5% change = Rs. 92.50

⇒ 18.5% of Cost Price = Rs. 92.50

⇒ Cost Price = 92.50 / (18.5/100) = Rs. 500

⇒ Selling Price for 12% profit = Cost Price × (1 + 12%)

⇒ Selling Price = 500 × (1 + 12%) = Rs. 560

questions.question: If the 8-digit number 2074x4y2 is divisible by 88, then the value of (4x + 3y) is:
questions.solution:
If 8 digit number 2074x4y2 is divisible by 88, the number will also be divisible by 8 and 11 both.

A number will be divisible by 8 if the last three digits of a number is divisible by 8.

The divisibility rule of 11 is that you must subtract and then add the digits in an alternating pattern from left to right. If your answer is 0 or 11 then it is divisible by 11.

⇒ 4y2 is divisible by 8 if y = 3 or 7

If y = 3, then

⇒ 2074x432 will be divisible by 11 if x = 9

If y = 7, then

⇒ 2074x472 is divisible by 11 if x = 5

Now we can say, if y = 3 then x = 9 and if y = 7, then x = 5

⇒ (4x + 3y)

⇒ (4 × 9 + 3 × 3) = 36 + 9 = 45

⇒ (4 × 5 + 3 × 7) = 20 + 21 = 41

When x is subtracted from each of 21, 22, 60 and 64, the numbers so obtained, in this order, are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between (x + 1) and (7x + 8)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

If x is subtracted from each of 21, 22, 60 and 64, then all number will be in proportion

According to the question

(21 – x) / (22 – x) = (60 – x) / (64 – x)

By Dividendo and Componendo

⇒ (21 – x + 22 – x) / (21 – x – 22 + x) = (60 – x + 64 – x) / (60 – x – 64 + x)

⇒ (43 – 2x) / (-1) = (124 – 2x) / (-4)

⇒ 172 – 8x = 124 – 2x

⇒ 6x = 48

⇒ x = 8

∴ Required mean proportional = √[(8 + 1) (7 × 8 + 8)] = √(9 × 64) = 24

questions.question: The average of thirteen numbers is 80. The average of the first five numbers is 74.5 and that of the next five numbers is 82.5. The 11th numbers is 6 more than the 12th number and the 12th number is 6 less than the 13th number. What is the average of the 11th and the 13th numbers?
questions.solution:
Average of 13 numbers = 80

⇒ Sum of 13 numbers = 80 × 13 = 1040

Average of the first 5 numbers = 74.5

⇒ Sum of the first 5 numbers = 74.5 × 5 = 372.5

Average of next five numbers (6th to 10th) = 82.5

⇒ Sum of the next five numbers (6th to 10th) = 82.5 × 5 = 412.5

⇒ Sum of the last 3 numbers = 1040 – 372.5 – 412.5 = 255

Let the 12th number be x.

11th numbers = x + 6 and 13th number = x + 6

According to the question

⇒ x + 6 + x + x + 6 = 255

⇒ x = 81

⇒ 11th number = x + 6 = 81 + 6 = 87

⇒ x + 6 = 81 + 6 = 87

∴ Average of 11th and 13th number = (87 + 87)/2 = 87

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 15,000 is lent at 16% p.a. compound interest. What is the difference between the compound interest for the second year and the third year?
questions.solution:
P = Rs. 15,000, r = 16%, T = 2 years

Compound interest only for 2ⁿd year

⇒ 15000 × (16/100) = 2400

⇒ 2400 × (16/100) = 384

Compound interest only for 2ⁿd year = 2400 + 384 = Rs. 2784

Compound interest only for 3rd year

⇒ 15000 × (16/100) = 2400 × 1 = 2400

⇒ 2400 × (16/100) = 384 × 2 = 768

⇒ 384 × (16/100) = 61.44

Compound interest of 3 years = 2400 + 768 + 61.44 = 3,229.44

∴ Required difference = 3,229.44 – 2,784 = Rs. 445.44

questions.question: If (8x³ – 27y³) ÷ (2x – 3y) = (Ax² + Bxy + Cy²), then the value of (2A + B – C) is:
questions.solution:
As we know, (a³ – b³) = (a – b) (a² + b² + ab)

⇒ (8x³ – 27y³) ÷ (2x – 3y)

⇒ [(2x)³ – (3y)³] ÷ (2x – 3y)

⇒ [(2x – 3y) {(2x)² + (3y)² + 2x × 3x}] ÷ (2x – 3y)

⇒ [4x² + 9y² + 6xy]

Comparing with (Ax² + Bxy + Cy²)

⇒ A = 4, B = 6 and C = 9

⇒ (2A + B – C) = 2 × 4 + 6 – 9 = 5

questions.question: The volume of a metallic cylindrical pipe is 7480 cm³. If its length is 1.4 m and its external radius is 9 cm, then its thickness (given π = 22/7) is:
questions.solution:
__GIven:__

Length of the cylinder (h) = 1.4 m = 140 cm, External radius of cylinder, R = 9 cm and internal radius of cylinder = r cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c33d7d27d51521201418bb29d454dffee007c201bb91054713e6307e6f7ab65.png] 

 

__Concept:__

Volume of solid cylinder, V_s=pi R²h

Volume of hollow cylinder, V_h=pi (R²-r²)h

__Calculation:__

Volume of hollow cylinder = V_h= pi (R²-r²)h

Rightarrow 7480=(22)/(7) times (9²-r²) times 140

Rightarrow(81-r²) = 17

⇒ r = 8 cm

∴ Thickness of the cylindrical pipe = R – r = 9 – 8 = 1 cm

questions.question: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB।।DC and its diagonals intersect at P. If AP = (3x – 1) cm, PC = (5x – 3) cm, BP = (2x + 1) cm and PD = (6x – 5) cm, then the length of DB is:
If ab + bc + ca = 8 and a² + b² + c² = 20, then a possible value of 1/2 × (a + b + c)[(a – b)² + (b – c)² + (c – a)²] is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ab + bc + ca = 8 and a² + b² + c² = 20

**Formula used:**

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)

**Calculation:**

(a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ (a + b + c)² = 20 + 2 × 8 = 36

⇒ (a + b + c) = 6

Now,

1/2 × (a + b + c)[(a – b)² + (b – c)² + (c – a)²]

⇒ 1/2(a + b + c)(a² + b² – 2ab + b2 + c2 – 2bc + c2 + a2 – 2ac) 

⇒ 1/2(a + b + c)[2(a2 + b2 + c2) – 2(ab + bc + ac)]

Now substituting the values,

⇒ (a + b + c)[(a2 + b2 + c2) – (ab + bc + ac)]

⇒ 6(20 – 8)

⇒ 6 × 12 = 72

**∴ The required answer is 72.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 40% more than their cost price and allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. His gain or loss percent is:
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of an article be 100x.

MP of an article = 100x × [140/100] = 140x

SP of an article = 140x × [75/100] = 105x

∴ Required profit percentage = [(105x – 100x)]/100x × 100 = 5%

questions.question: The income of A is 50% more than that of B. If the income of A is increased by 40% and the income of B is increased by 90%, then the percentage increased in their combined income will be:
questions.solution:
Let the income of B be 100x.

Income of A = 100x × [150/100] = 150x

Sum of their income = 100x + 150x = 250x

New income of A = 150x × [140/100] = 210x

New income of B = 100x × [190/100] = 190x

Sum of their New income = 210x + 190x = 400x

∴ Required percentage = [(400x – 250x)/250x] × 100 = 60%
